analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, high-ROCE (26.5%) IT services micro-cap trading at a PEG of ~0.3 (P/E 8.91 vs 5Y earnings CAGR 39%) — classic Lynch GARP territory on the surface. But the story is cracking: FY25 revenue grew only ~2% (98→100 Cr) and operating income fell from 34 to 30 Cr, so I'd wait for re-acceleration before buying.
key_strengths: PEG ~0.3 (P/E 8.91 vs 5Y PAT CAGR 39%) — textbook GARP math
Zero borrowings, ROE 20%, ROCE 26.5% — clean high-quality compounder
OCF positive 5/5 years; equity ₹171 Cr ≈ 84% of ₹203 Cr mcap, downside cushioned
key_risks: Growth stalled in FY25: revenue +2%, EBIT down 12% — the thesis is weakening
Micro-cap IT services shop competing with thousands of global vendors — no visible moat
₹77 Cr investing outflow in FY25 post-IPO; capital allocation of new cash unproven
red_flags: Operating margin compression in FY25 (OI 34→30 Cr) despite higher revenue base
Recent IPO (reserves jumped 46→147 Cr in 2025) — short public track record
Low FII/DII ownership (<6% combined) — limited institutional validation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On paper this is a Lynch dream: a small IT consulting shop (₹203 Cr mcap) growing earnings ~39% CAGR over five years, ROCE 26.5%, zero debt, and trading at under 9x earnings — PEG of roughly 0.3. Promoter holds 74.67%, skin in the game is intact. Revenue CAGR of 28% from ₹29 Cr to ₹100 Cr shows real execution, and the business converts earnings to cash cleanly (FCF positive every year, ₹18 Cr in FY25).

The problem is that the growth story — which is everything in a Lynch framework — is decelerating sharply right at the point I'd want to buy. FY24→FY25 revenue went 98→100 (basically flat), operating income actually contracted from 34 to 30 Cr, and most of the "net profit" stability was propped up by a jump in other income (0→6 Cr, likely IPO cash parked in treasury). IT services is a brutally competitive space with no niche dominance here, and a sub-scale ₹100 Cr revenue vendor has no pricing power. I'd keep it on the watchlist, wait one or two quarters for top-line to re-accelerate above 15%, and then revisit — if growth returns, the cheap PEG could make this a multi-bagger; if it doesn't, the cheap optics are a value trap.
